summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted with right lower quadrant pain, fever, and nausea two weeks after laparoscopic appendectomy. CT imaging revealed a periappendiceal abscess, which was successfully drained percutaneously under CT guidance. She was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and transitioned to oral antibiotics (ciprofloxacin and metronidazole). Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home after three days with instructions to complete a 10-day antibiotic course and follow up in two weeks for repeat imaging. Her psychiatric and chronic medical conditions were maintained on home medications without complication.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
